newsitem.title: USA: American Classic bookings outlook positive.
newsitem.headline: American Classic bookings outlook positive.

text.p: American Classic Voyages Co, which operates two U.S. flag cruise lines, said Tuesday the outlook for bookings for 1997 remains positive.
"The company's 1997 booking outlook remains positive," said Philip Calian, chief executive officer.

"Currently Delta Queen is approximately 74 percent booked at a rate of $279 per passenger night for 1997 and American Hawaii is 76 percent booked at a rate of $213 per passenger night, per diems well head of 1996 levels," he said in a statement.

Earlier today, American Classic reported a 1997 first quarter loss of about $2 million or $0.14 a share, in line with the company's expectations. "Our operating loss for this period, historically our weakest quarter, is the smallest it has been for the past four years and represents a continuation of our 1996 positive earnings trend," he said.
Shares of American Classic were trading up 1/4 to 10-1/8.
